subject: Intermittent checkout slowdowns — executive escalation requested
messages:
From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@atlasretail.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: support@atlasretail.com
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent large completion delays impacting checkout

Hi Marissa,

We started seeing a pattern this morning where a subset of checkout predictions (fractions of a percent) are taking 10-30x longer than normal to complete and some are returning 502s. Our daily p95 looks fine but p99.9 and tail completion time have spiked; throughput to the endpoint has dropped by ~18% while error rate climbed to 1.6%.

This is customer-facing and impacting the payment confirmation flow. Attached is a sample of requests and a CSV of p99 traces from our side. We're running on your hosted endpoint (region: us-west) with a pinned model version.

Can you escalate to your engineering leadership and advise immediate mitigation steps? We need an interim workaround (routing, concurrency cap change, or fallback) and an ETA for a full fix.

We can make ourselves available for a 30-minute bridge if needed.

Thanks,
Emma Jones
Head of Platform Integrations
Atlas Retail
Attachment: request-sample-20280301.json (application/json)
Attachment: p99-trace-20280301.csv (text/csv)

Emma — thank you for the quick heads up and for the samples. I'm looping in Ben (account lead) and Hannah/Dylan from CS + Infra to triage immediately.

Immediate actions we will take in the next 30–45 minutes:
- Open a debug bridge and correlate the supplied request IDs with our request logs.
- Temporarily enable a conservative fallback route to the previous model variant to reduce error rate if we observe timeouts at the model runtime layer.
- Check for any recent routing changes, autoscaler events, or network flaps in the us-west region.

Hannah/Dylan — can you confirm whether there's any active concurrency capping or sustained KV-cache thrashing for Atlas' tenant? If so, let's evaluate a temporary cap increase and routing to Dedicated pools as a mitigation.

Emma — I'll update you within 45 minutes with next steps and a proposal for an exec-level sync if we can't stabilize quickly.

—Marissa

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 3 Mar 2028 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent large completion delays impacting checkout

Quick incident update and ask for exec decision:

What we found so far:
- Root correlation points to intermittent backpressure at the serving pool where Atlas' shard is colocated. The autoscaler showed a burst of worker restarts between 07:45–08:10 PT on 2028-03-01, creating transient KV-cache churn and elevated tail latencies.
- We reproduced the pattern in a controlled replay; when concurrency on a worker hits the configured soft cap the scheduler briefly queues requests instead of spawning additional warm workers, producing long-tail queueing for a small fraction of traffic.
- No code-level regression discovered; rather a tuning interaction between scheduler soft-cap and the new packing heuristic pushed too many tenants onto a few workers during a resource transient.

Immediate mitigation already applied:
- Increased soft concurrency cap for Atlas' shard from 30 -> 48 (temporary) and enabled the fallback model variant routing for 1 hour. Error rate dropped to 0.15% and throughput returned to baseline in canary.
- Captured a replay bundle (customer-replay-logs-0301.tar.gz) and uploaded it to INF-6729.

Decision needed from execs (Laura/CTO):
- Approve a 48-hour Dedicated routing option for Atlas while we implement a conservative scheduler fix and a safer packing policy. Estimated incremental cost: ~ $12k/day.
- Approve a 10% goodwill credit against March usage if Atlas elects to continue on Hosted rather than Dedicated (customer retention risk).

If approved, we'll pivot traffic and schedule an emergency deploy to harden scheduler heuristics (target: 48h). Otherwise we will continue with fallback routing and periodic cap increases which are operationally risky.

Next steps: I can brief Laura and the CTO immediately if Ben confirms exec availability.

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Customer Reliability Engineering
